title: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel after Trump export ban threat
description: The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel in a bid to ease supply pressures that have caused prices to skyrocket.The group of
body: The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel in a bid to ease supply pressures that have caused prices to skyrocket.The group of advanced economies, including the US, said the move would include a "substantial release" of diesel in the coming days.President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports in a move which would have eased pressure on prices for US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections, but pushed up prices elsewhere.In a joint statement, the G7 said member countries had now agreed to "refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products" on one another.The G7 includes the US, UK, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France, with the EU also represented at its meetings.Trump had warned he would ban diesel exports from the US if European countries did not agree to put more of their own stocks onto the market.On Friday, he said on social media: "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately."His Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had argued US farmers, truckers, and businesses "should not be left carrying the burden" as prices soar.Diesel is used heavily by the haulage industry and in agriculture, meaning rises in the cost of the fuel feed through into essentials such as food.But, following a meeting of G7 leaders, French President Emmanuel Macron said the bloc had agreed to release reserves of "up to 100 million barrels" within four months under the co-ordination of the International Energy Agency (IEA).The UK was represented at the meeting by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who said the measures would "stabilise energy supplies, build resilience in supply chains and shield households and businesses from price shocks".Macron said the co-ordinated action would "bring down the prices of petroleum products, particularly diesel". Highlighting the agreement not to pursue export bans, Macron said "President Trump, in particular, was very clear on this point". Speaking at the White House, Trump later said an export ban on diesel was "never really on the table". In the joint statement, G7 leaders said: "We will implement our commitments with a co-ordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over four months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G7 members and partners." It is not yet clear which partner countries will release stocks, nor how quickly.The 100 million barrels will comprise a mix of diesel and crude oil. The price of global benchmark Brent crude oil briefly dropped below $100 a barrel, but rose back to around $102 by Friday evening. Before the US and Israel invaded Iran, it was trading at around $73.Matt Smith, director of commodities research at Kpler, said oil had risen again due to renewed strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen."Oil prices were selling off strongly due to the announcement of strategic stock releases in Europe, but they reversed course on rumours of Saudi Arabia planning an offensive into Yemen as it looks to re-establish a safe path via Bab-Al Mandeb," he said.European countries had pushed back against US threats to turn off American diesel, against a backdrop of the US-led war in the Middle East and reduced supplies from Russia and China.The G7 leaders said they will also co-ordinate maintenance schedules to avoid multiple refineries being shut down at the same time, while encouraging countries with the capacity to do so to ramp up refining of diesel in particular. Supplies of diesel internationally have been heavily constrained by the conflict in the Middle East, which has restricted the flow of both crude oil and refined diesel onto global markets.Russia, which is also a major producer, has implemented its own export ban on diesel, following attacks on its refineries by Ukraine, further limiting supply. The G7 leaders stressed that they will maintain sanctions against Russia amid its ongoing war in Ukraine. Diesel is harder to refine than petrol and, because of its use in the haulage industry and agriculture, it is very difficult to reduce demand.

schema.headline: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel after Trump export ban threat

title: Women given free shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting
description: One woman made €9,000 (£7,650) from a single clip, according to BR, whose investigations found that a group of professional YouTubers from Ukraine and
body: One woman made €9,000 (£7,650) from a single clip, according to BR, whose investigations found that a group of professional YouTubers from Ukraine and several people from Bavaria were behind the videos.At least 32,000 videos of women on the Teufelsrad have been in circulation, according to Munich-based daily Süddeutsche Zeitung. Some have apparently been viewed millions of times.The operator of the Teufelsrad, Elisabeth Polaczy, told the BBC that, for the past three years, she has been handing out free cycling shorts to women and girls wearing dresses, to protect them from people filming in the crowd.This Oktoberfest she has handed out more than 100 pairs, she says: "I want to do everything I can to make people feel secure."Polaczy, who is now 80, said donating cycling shorts wasn't cheap, but it was worth it for her own peace of mind. The Teufelsrad tent is hung with signs and police posters in German and English warning against filming under people's skirts, but Polaczy says it is impossible to control everyone filming with smart phones.Some waitresses at this year's beer festival say they have also started wearing cycling shorts under their dirndls.A spokesman for the Bavarian police told the BBC that since 2025, it has run a poster campaign at the Oktoberfest, warning against upskirting.This year, police arrested a 45-year-old Swiss man for using his phone to film under a German woman's dirndl. Last year there were 10 arrests for upskirting and seven in 2024.However, Josephine Ballon, who heads German non-profit organisation Hate Aid,  which aims to support victims of digital violence, told the BBC that the current law against upskirting does not provide enough protection.Although she says there are plans for a new law, current legislation "applies only when you film under the skirt", and not when a skirt simply flies up and gets photographed. The new camera glasses are also a threat, she believes.Ballon wants anyone who has uploaded intimate pictures of women on the internet to be punished, along with the platforms that put them up.Meanwhile, the city of Munich has sought to tighten up on influencers and content creators who earn money from their social media postings and who want to film at the Oktoberfest.Munich has banned broadcasting live streams from the festival and requires anyone who wants to film there to hold a permit, which is issued by the city for a fee.Hundreds of licences have been issued this year to influencers, who make money from product placement or sponsoring.

schema.headline: Women given free shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

title: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry 'failed' by officials, says New York governor
description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said the woman at the centre of the Cornell University rape case was "failed" at "every turn". The woman, known as
body: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said the woman at the centre of the Cornell University rape case was "failed" at "every turn". The woman, known as Jane Doe in legal documents, alleges she was drugged and raped by several men at a fraternity house in 2024. The case was investigated at the time but no charges were laid. It recently reopened after the woman filed a civil lawsuit last month that thrust the allegations into the national spotlight. At a news conference on Friday, Hochul said she was "deeply disturbed" by how the investigation was handled. She has now appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to lead the case. This appointment was made after Hochul said she "lost faith" in the local prosecutor's ability to oversee the investigation.Expressing outrage that local prosecutors did not interview the accuser themselves,  Hochul on Friday said: "This young woman had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable, and then at every turn she was failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her."She has also vowed to close a "loophole" that prevents prosecutors from pursuing rape charges in cases when the victim has voluntarily consumed drugs or alcohol. Jane Doe is believed to have voluntarily taken drugs and alcohol on the night of the alleged gang rape."If someone is too intoxicated to consent it should not matter if they chose to use drugs or alcohol," said Hochul, adding: "Voluntary intoxication is not a licence for gang rape."James, who is the state's chief legal officer, appeared alongside Hochul at Friday's news conference, pledging to "lead a process guided by the facts and the law".She said her office would interview witnesses and pursue prosecutions if warranted.District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who previously led the investigation, has defended his office's previous decision not to file charges in the case, arguing they were not given enough evidence to meet the legal threshold.Van Houten said much of the information released in recent weeks about the case was not passed to his office. In a statement on Friday, he said he supported James' investigation, adding: "It has become clear that we were not provided the full picture by the university."Cornell has said it provided evidence to the district attorney's office from its own investigation, including a Snapchat group chat in which fraternity members discussed a "free" sexual encounter with Doe on the night of the alleged assault.Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university in September.Speaking to CNN on Friday, her lawyer Thomas Giuffra said she is "not doing well"."She's under siege on social media, where people are trying to identify her; some false court postings, attempting to identify her," he said. Survivor and victim advocates say current state law on sexual assault makes it difficult for charges to be brought against perpetrators if the victim voluntarily took drugs or drank alcohol before the alleged assault took place.A bill to address what Hochul described as a legal loophole was already before the state legislature prior to this week's public outcry over how police and investigators handled the Cornell rape allegations. People who have voluntarily become intoxicated to the point that they are unable to give consent are currently not protected by New York's rape laws, says state assemblyman Jeffrey Dinowitz, who first sponsored legislation to close the loophole in 2019."The real bottom line is that right now if you are voluntarily intoxicated, you will not get justice," he tells BBC News. "Being voluntarily intoxicated, basically, is almost like giving somebody a get out of jail free card."Dinowitz says that around half of US states have already changed their laws to say it makes no difference whether intoxication is voluntarily or involuntarily in rape cases.Hochul said she will support the existing bill and that it could move forward as early as the next legislative session which reconvenes in January. As governor, she could also call lawmakers back for a special session before then.

schema.headline: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry 'failed' by officials, says New York governor

title: Intensified Russian strikes are tearing Kyiv apart, Klitschko warns
description: "We're talking about survival," Klitschko said at Friday's defence council meeting with Kyiv's top military, security, emergencies and police official
body: "We're talking about survival," Klitschko said at Friday's defence council meeting with Kyiv's top military, security, emergencies and police officials.Russia's aim was to "sow panic", he said, stressing that the capital would "prevail - but only through the joint efforts of those who love it and care for it".The mayor was speaking just hours after Kyiv's key Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was hit in an overnight Russian drone attack. On Friday evening it was struck again - the fourth time in two days.The bridge is one of the main transport arteries across the Dnipro River dividing western and eastern parts of Kyiv.All metro and automobile traffic is now suspended across the bridge, causing major delays across the city. Restrictions are also in place on Kyiv's two other key bridges.Kyiv's current population is estimated to be about three million, and many residents rely heavily on the city's metro network. One person was killed in the capital when a multi-storey residential building was hit overnight, Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS said.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Putin had decided in early September that "there are no rules now" when attacking Ukraine.In a published excerpt from his interview with the Financial Times, Zelensky said: "The Russians have failed to occupy us. So now they are carrying out massive attacks and mass killings. "They want to destroy our bridges... our data centres, the internet, mobile networks, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, universities - everything. They want people to flee their cities."Putin insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries and its ships in the Black Sea."Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," Putin said after a wide-ranging speech at the Valdai foreign policy forum on Thursday.Putin admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helps the Kremlin finance the war.Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure, ramping up attacks every winter since Putin launched a full-scale invasion in 2022.

schema.headline: Intensified Russian strikes are tearing Kyiv apart, Klitschko warns

title: Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after botched execution, lawyer says
description: Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her botched execution.Hospital staff are working to s
body: Pike's lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her botched execution.Hospital staff are working to save her life and clear the drug used, pentobarbital, from her system, the filing states.During the execution attempt, prison officials tried to start intravenous (IV) lines by using at least seven needles on Pike, according to her lawyers.At one point, Pike herself offered guidance of where they could try."One needle was bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed," the filing states.While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent review into Pike's botched execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.The state's department of correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".Authorities are yet to say whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have not not offered any explanations about what went wrong.Pike's attorneys previously warned that her conditions, including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.In the latest filings, her lawyers allege that "at no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms Pike's body".They are requesting that all relevant physical, written and electronic evidence is preserved.Dr Joel Zivot, an anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team, said two doses of pentobarbital was enough that "she would have surely died" had it entered her bloodstream in normal circulation.The only possible explanation for her survival, Zivot said, "is that the pentobarbital blood level was never high enough to cause death" and that blisters on her arm after the botched execution indicated a ruptured vein.So, instead of entering Pike's bloodstream, he said, the pentobarbital was more likely to have spread across the tissue under her skin.Pike's medical condition of thrombocytosis may have also played a role, forming blood clots at the injection site that would potentially block pentobarbital from entering her veins.Regarding the possibility the pentobarbital was degraded, Zivot explained that if this was the case, it could be due to factors including poor manufacturing or improper storage.

schema.headline: Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after botched execution, lawyer says

title: Rui Pinto: Hacker who released Man City documents fears for life as he prepares to lose witness protection
description: Pinto became part of Portugal's witness protection programme in 2020 after agreeing to co-operate with authorities and provide files obtained through
body: Pinto became part of Portugal's witness protection programme in 2020 after agreeing to co-operate with authorities and provide files obtained through the Football Leaks operation.He posted on X on Friday, external that the decision to terminate his participation in the programme on 10 October has put him in a "life-threatening situation".The 37-year-old said it had left him with no alternative but to relocate to an undisclosed location for an indefinite period because of "multiple death threats" and "the serious risk of an assassination attempt".BBC Sport has approached the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Crimes in Portugal for comment.Pinto has described himself as a whistleblower, but was convicted in Portugal of offences including illegal access to data and attempted extortion and given a four-year suspended sentence.He wore a bulletproof vest during his first trial in 2020, which was also subject to heightened security measures.Earlier this year, he was acquitted in a second trial of 241 counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to a number of sports bodies in Portugal, including Benfica.On Wednesday, Pinto turned his attention to Fifa president Gianni Infantino, saying he had "become a cancer on football" and should "have no place in the future of the game".Pinto repeated allegations from 2018 that Infantino intervened to help City and Paris St-Germain avoid financial fair play sanctions from European football's governing body Uefa.Infantino's position has recently come under increased pressure following controversial plans to sell stakes in the governing body's competitions, such as the World Cup, to private investors. A statement from Pinto's lawyers released on Friday said the decision to end his participation in the witness protection programme left him at heightened risk, noting legal proceedings stemming from the leaks remained ongoing, including the case against Manchester City.Pinto has set up a fundraising page to help him "survive this serious situation", which he claims was "created by the Portuguese State".

schema.headline: Rui Pinto: Hacker who released Man City documents fears for life as he prepares to lose witness protection

title: Spoilers: Is social media ruining gig surprises?
description: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises? Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Big moments from Olivia Rodrigo's tour were dissect
body: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises? Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Big moments from Olivia Rodrigo's tour were dissected online shortly after her opening night BySrosh Khan and Riyah CollinsBBC NewsbeatMonths before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.  You'll also probably know the set list, the stage design, and - if you've really been paying attention - where to stand to get the best view. When it comes to films and TV series, spoilers tend to be guarded against with warnings.But for many major gigs, there's no escaping a stream of fan videos from the shows if you're online, whether you like it or not.Last week, US pop star Olivia Rodrigo kicked off her Unraveled tour, and surprises from the show, which scores of fans have paid a lot of money to see, have already been dissected online.Tours by Harry Styles, Charli XCX and Ariana Grande have also been filmed from every angle and shared over the past few months.While some fans lap up the opportunity to see what's coming, others are taking extreme measures to preserve the element of surprise. Image source, HandoutImage caption, Aurélia Collins always aims to go to gigs not knowing what to expectAurélia Collins is one of them, spending weeks trying to trick her algorithm into not serving her content about her favourite artists and tapping "not interested" when videos come up, even though she says "it hurts my soul". It can mean her social media feed is a bit bland, but she tells BBC Newsbeat "it's worth it for the surprise".The 20-year-old criminology student is a huge One Direction fan and says she just about managed to avoid spoilers for Styles' Together, Together tour over summer. But when one slipped through the net about Niall Horan before she was able to see his show in London on Saturday - her first time seeing him live after being a fan for 16 years - she was "gutted"."When I was younger, we couldn't afford to go to events like this and hear live music and because it's such a moment, I really want to take it in," she says."I want the full experience, and that includes the element of surprise that people that go to the opening night of the tour can get."Image source, HandoutImage caption, Georgia McAdam says videos online help her plan her gig experience Not all fans think spoilers are a bad thing, though. In fact, Georgia McAdam claims she loves them."I'm the type of person that loves to be prepared," the 22-year-old says. "I love to know what the stage is looking like, what the set list consists of and where to stand."McAdam's a huge Olivia Rodrigo fan and sees online spoilers more as "teasers". She feels no amount of online videos can ever really take away from the excitement of the real thing. "Sometimes you get different surprise songs to what's online or you never know what an artist might do," she adds.'You have to not look at TikTok'Some artists have reacted by switching up their sets in small ways each night to make sure fans coming to later dates still see something unexpected. Taylor Swift had bespoke outfits and surprise songs during her mammoth Eras tour, Sabrina Carpenter performed unique positions during her song Juno and switched up her Nonsense outro, and Jay-Z has been changing up his set list on his current run.But the Guardian's deputy music editor Laura Snapes says it's not just fans who can benefit from these twists. "One way that they can make sure they're staying in the press is by having something different happen in their show every night," Snapes says. "Obviously, it'll be all over TikTok."Figures shared by TikTok with Newsbeat show posts using #CharliXCX have increased by more than 40% since the singer launched her Music, Fashion, Film tour last month. If you want to avoid spoilers, there's only one thing you can do, according to Snapes: "You have to not look at TikTok."If you want to be surprised, you have to protect yourself from absorbing any of that culture."Image source, Getty Images for AEGImage caption, Have you ever tried this one? Sabrina Carpenter had a number of special reveals for each show on her Short n' Sweet tourPhoebe Bridgers is taking things one step further to make sure fans are surprised at her shows - she's banning phones altogether.Those attending are required to lock their phones and any recording devices in a special pouch when they enter the venue to see the US singer. Anyone found breaking the rules will be escorted out. McAdam wouldn't support a ban on phones, saying recording at gigs is "part of the experience" for a lot of fans.But Collins says she's "not totally against it".What she'd prefer is to see more spoiler warnings on videos so fans have the option to be surprised if they want.But even if you know the set list, the staging and the outfits, "you're still probably going to get to see moments of humanity and stuff that's unplanned," Snapes adds. "I went to the Edinburgh Eras show where Taylor Swift was really snotty and she had to blow her nose. That's not part of the script."You're always going to be surprised."Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here.

schema.headline: Spoilers: Is social media ruining gig surprises?

title: Man jailed for piloting small boat carrying 26 others to Kent coast
description: A man has been jailed for 18 months for piloting a small boat carrying 26 other people, including six children, towards the Kent coast. Jemal Abdela,
body: A man has been jailed for 18 months for piloting a small boat carrying 26 other people, including six children, towards the Kent coast. Jemal Abdela, 32, was sentenced after pleading guilty to the offence of endangering others during a sea crossing to the UK without valid entry clearance on July 25.Winchester Crown Court heard Abdela, who is Eritrean, had also attempted to disguise the fact he had been driving the black inflatable across the Channel when it was approached by immigration officers.A Home Office spokesman said Abdela was the 20th small boat pilot to be imprisoned in four months for endangering lives at sea.Matthew Parris, prosecuting, told the court that the defendant was seen piloting the boat, which was being followed by French authorities.He said Abdela had "dived into the centre of the boat and moved to another location wearing a hat" before being identified, adding that the vessel did not have flares, GPS or maps onboard.The court heard that Abdela told police he had paid €800 (£680) for the crossing, which had begun at 17:00 BST the previous day.He also claimed to have been sat by the captain of the boat, but was then made to take over control of the vessel by the other passengers.Francesca Hallett, defending, said that Abdela had managed to "escape" war-torn Eritrea, where he was born.She said that he first went to the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, but was imprisoned because of his Eritrean nationality.He then went on to travel through Sudan and Egypt to Libya where he was captured and tortured by people smugglers for eight months and was later freed.Hallett added that Abdela moved on to Italy and France, both of which he described as "not safe for refugees"."At that stage he felt the UK was the safest option," she said.Sentencing Abdela, Judge James Bromige said that he would "ordinarily" be deported on completion of his time in prison.Anna Turley, Minister for Border Security and Asylum, called Abdela a "reckless criminal" who had been "rightly jailed".Additional reporting by PA Media Follow BBC Kent on Facebook, external,  X, external, and on Instagram, external and listen to BBC Radio Kent on Sounds. Send your story ideas to southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk, external or WhatsApp us on 08081 002250.

title: Daniel Thomas in court accused of entering Dover migrant site
description: Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has appeared in court charged with entering a restricted zone at a migrant processing centre in Dover.The 37-year-
body: Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has appeared in court charged with entering a restricted zone at a migrant processing centre in Dover.The 37-year-old, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, is accused of committing the offence on 31 March, according to court documents.Thomas is further accused of using threatening words or behaviour in the Kent town on 1 April and obstructing a person engaged in a lawful activity on 6 April.He is also charged with entering or remaining in Dover Docks without having lawful business or permission, the documents say.Thomas faces another charge of racially aggravated harassment by allegedly using threatening or abusive words.He appeared at Margate Magistrates' Court on Friday via videolink wearing a grey T-shirt and rosary beads.District Judge William Nelson sent his case for a further case management hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court on 4 November.Earlier this week, Thomas was refused bail during a crown court hearing over the alleged slashing of a dinghy in the English Channel.Follow BBC Kent on Facebook, external, on X, external, and on Instagram, external and listen to BBC Radio Kent on Sounds. title: Celebrity Traitors claim their first victim as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin
description: Image caption, Maya Jama is off to a strong start as a traitor, but Richard E Grant is in damage control modeBySteven McIntoshEntertainment reporter S
body: Image caption, Maya Jama is off to a strong start as a traitor, but Richard E Grant is in damage control modeBySteven McIntoshEntertainment reporter Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment."It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day."But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."The next morning, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.Image caption, It was the end of the road for Amol Rajan, who noted he had perhaps been "a bit bullish" in challening GrantThe 69-year-old spent much of Friday's episode trying to repair the damage from his earlier exchange in the bar, where he blurted out that he was a traitor to Joe Lycett, Rob Beckett and several others.Obviously a man who made such an excellent Spice Girls manager in the 1997 masterpiece Spice World: The Movie is hard for anyone to picture as a traitor, so many other players assumed Grant was attempting some elaborate double bluff.Jama is off to a much stronger start. "I am quite shocked at my ability to just lie to everyone," the Love Island host said in the castle's diary room. "I'm an all-or-nothing kind of honey."As the players gathered for breakfast, other theories began to surface. Mathematician Hannah Fry said she had spotted Leigh-Anne Pinnock putting on make-up late in the evening, perhaps heading to the turret."I think it's James," declared Jerry Hall, suddenly giving viewers hope that the new cast will be better traitor hunters than last year's. Until she clarified that she was talking about James Blunt, not Acaster.As the players prepared to head out for the mission, conversations turned to far more important matters. "Do you have more teeth than a normal person?" Grant asked Rob Beckett.Figure caption, Watch: Richard E. Grant hits back at Rob Beckett in The Celebrity TraitorsThe players made their way to the mission, which had the usual slightly convoluted rules that took Winkleman quite a while to explain.In a nutshell, the celebrities were to be buried alive in pairs, with only one duo left above ground.Ross Kemp was pre-selected by the traitors to be protected from burial along with his grave partner Romesh Ranganathan, who did a delightful dance when he found out he wouldn't be going underground.Kemp and Ranganathan then had the opportunity to dig up some gold graves which would add to the prize pot, or alternatively dig up and free their fellow players.They opted for the latter, which resulted in some other players struggling, external to get the soil off their faces. In the end, all the celebrities were released, with the exception of Fry and Hall.The pair were freed early after Hall shouted the emergency word "Haggis!" – effectively a Scottish version of "I'm a celebrity get me out of here!" - because she was visibly uncomfortable being buried alive.It might have led to an early release, but it ultimately guaranteed that either she or Fry will be murdered next, unless the traitors recruit again."Just you and me up for murder," Fry told Hall afterwards. "You'd better not be a traitor or I'm really screwed!"In a flashback shown to viewers, Acaster explained the decision to protect Kemp from burial, telling his fellow traitors: "I think if we give it to Ross, he'll overthink it, and behave in a way that would draw suspicion."Very clever. "You're a wonderful traitor," observed Grant. (Certainly better than him.)Image caption, Ranganathan began dancing when he found out he would be protected from burial along with KempImage caption, Jerry Hall and Hannah Fry face being murdered after Hall requested to be freed from the grave earlyFinally, it was time for the first banishment of the series, with Grant still in damage control mode."I have a slight pinprick of advantage," he told himself in the castle's diary room. "Nobody would possibly believe that anybody would be so stupid as to come forward and say 'I am a traitor'. I'm hoping that I do get away with it."His fellow traitors clearly wanted to be supportive, but things were getting dicey. Acaster described him as a "loose cannon", while Jama said: "I want to save him, even though he's dug himself the biggest hole imaginable."Back in the castle, Ranganathan pointed out: "If somebody else had behaved like Richard, we wouldn't even be having a debate about this, you would just go 'you've got to vote for him'."But others had a slightly different take. "Richard feels a little too easy," reflected actress Myha'la, "and then anybody pushing him feels suspicious to me."Comedian Joanne McNally agreed some players were "using him as a fall guy and a decoy," although she did admit later that he's "made such a shambles of it now".Image caption, Julie Hesmondhalgh (with James Blunt, left, and King Kenny) argued for Grant to be banishedAs discussions got going, it took a surprisingly long time for Grant's name to come up, as the other players debated other suspects such as Julie Hesmondhalgh.The actress aroused suspicion because she was the first celebrity this year to receive a shield. The group seemed to have overlooked she only got that - in the opening minutes of the first show - after the other contestants voted her the most trustworthy.But as discussion turned to Grant, Hesmondhalgh put forward one of the most convincing cases of the night."You came into the bar, and said you were a traitor," she told him. "It was a bold move. It was chaotic and we love you for your chaos."I think we are at risk of being the most idiotic group of faithfuls in the world, if we go for someone else tonight based on nothing at all, when somebody has come into the room and said 'I am a traitor'. There's no reason to say it unless you are."Miranda Hart agreed that "the joy when he took off his blindfold" when Winkleman first selected the traitors made Grant look suspicious.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Newly recruited traitor James Acaster looks set to last longer than Richard E GrantViewers will have to wait until the next episode to see how the round table goes, as the episode finished before voting had even started.(It's worth saying that, as cliffhangers go, this was far less irritating than ending an episode in the middle of a roundtable, as producers often do.)"You've given us all a problem," Ranganathan told Grant as the episode drew to a close and the players prepared to vote. "By doing that, it was a big mistake by you, I feel like you forced our hand."Admittedly, it's not looking good - the round table is shaping up to be a landslide vote against Grant. But we still wouldn't bet against him. "I do not go down without a fight," he concluded. "I couldn't have survived showbusiness for four decades without a fight."Celebrity Traitors continues on Thursday at 20:00 BST on BBC One and iPlayer.

schema.headline: Celebrity Traitors claim their first victim as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin

title: Beijing Open: Aryna Sabalenka 'expects a bit more from myself' after win over Renata Zarazua
description: Aryna Sabalenka said she was "trying so hard to be easier on myself" as she began her China Open campaign with victory over Renata Zarazua.World numbe
body: Aryna Sabalenka said she was "trying so hard to be easier on myself" as she began her China Open campaign with victory over Renata Zarazua.World number two Sabalenka hit 11 aces and did not face a break point in a 6-1 6-3 victory over the Mexican.The Belarusian needed just 63 minutes to win her first match since losing her world number one ranking and her US Open crown to Elena Rybakina in September.The 28-year-old is bidding for her first title since completing the 'Sunshine Double' in March, when she won Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back.It has been a mixed year for Sabalenka by her high standards. She will finish without a Grand Slam trophy for the first time since 2022 and has often struggled to control her frustrations on court.Asked about being so self-critical, Sabalenka said: "I think this is a good and a bad side of my personality, that I always ask and wait for more from myself. "Sometimes it can drive me forward, but sometimes it can really drain my energy."Maybe this is something I have to finally learn. I'm really trying so hard sometimes to be easier on myself."Sabalenka will face Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova - who came close to beating her at the Berlin Open in June - in the third round.Top seed Rybakina begins her campaign at the WTA 1000 event on Saturday.Earlier, Britain's Katie Boulter fell 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 to Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova, while French Open champion Mirra Andreeva recovered to beat Chinese wildcard Yuan Yue 3-6 6-0 6-0.In the men's event, sixth seed Daniil Medvedev produced 12 aces to beat Spain's Pablo Carreno Busta 6-4 6-2.British pair Julian Cash and Lloyd Glasspool advanced in the doubles, beating Russia's Andrey Rublev and Karen Khachanov 6-3 6-4.

title: The Prem: Bath 40-34 Exeter: Bath beat Chiefs in 11-try thriller
description: The PremBath (26) 40Tries: Redpath, van der Linde, du Preez, Russell, Penalty, Hill Cons: Russell 4 Exeter (10) 34Tries: Varney, Yeandle, Iosefa-Scott
body: The PremBath (26) 40Tries: Redpath, van der Linde, du Preez, Russell, Penalty, Hill Cons: Russell 4 Exeter (10) 34Tries: Varney, Yeandle, Iosefa-Scott, Feyi-Waboso 2 Cons: Slade 3 Pen: Skinner Bath made it two wins out of two in the new Prem season as they gained a degree of revenge for losing to Exeter Chiefs in last season's semi-final.The two sides produced another thrilling game, just as they did three months ago, exchanging 11 tries as the all-out attack approach to the new season continued.     The hosts scored four tries to have a bonus point in the bag by the break as Cameron Redpath, Bernard van der Linde, Dan du Preez and Finn Russell all scored to put them 26-10 ahead.Stephen Varney and Jack Yeandle had got Exeter's first-half scores, before Josh Iosefa-Scott and two great tries from England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso turned the match on its head within 15 minutes of the restart.But Varney gave up a penalty try for a deliberate knock-on and Ted Hill's effort took the game beyond their opponents, although Harvey Skinner kicked a late penalty to ensure the visitors came away from a second consecutive defeat with two bonus points.The last meeting between the pair at the same venue is a match that will be remembered forever as the Chiefs came from 16 points down at half-time to win their Prem semi-final by a single point.That defeat dethroned Bath as champions and they were looking ruthless as they grabbed two early tries.Redpath read Skinner's intentions to make an interception at point-blank range, giving him a free run to the line from inside his own half and there was opportunism about Bath's second score, as scrum-half van der Linde spotted a gap, dummied and sprinted over from just outside the 22.Exeter had to respond and Feyi-Waboso's burst near the corner drew in enough defenders to allow Varney to exploit space to get his side on the board.However, they could not keep the hosts out for long with more livewire stuff from van der Linde at the heart of it as he combined with Ewan Richards and although the little South African was held up a few metres short, there was no stopping compatriot du Preez from that distance.A simple maul from a line-out saw Chiefs hooker Yeandle dot it down for their second try, but Bath had their bonus point on half-time as they worked the ball back to Russell with a bit of space and the Scotland and Lions fly-half did the rest with a dummy, turn of pace and finish.With Russell converting his own try, it left an identical half-time score to that sunny June afternoon and just as they did three months ago, Rob Baxter's side came storming back and within 15 minutes, they had turned a 16-point deficit into a five-point advantage.A powerful drive by Kane James punctured a hole in Bath's defence with Iosefa-Scott eventually able to pick and go for the prop's second try in two games.Then it was Feyi-Waboso's turn to come to the party as he cut a devastating line from outside to in after a huge floated pass from Skinner found him on the touchline.And his second try arrived thanks to great support play after ex-Bath centre Will Butt danced his way through a gap in midfield to open up the game.But unlike last time, Bath found a response as their reinforcements from the bench added grunt. Redpath spilled the ball with the line beckoning but as they kept the pressure on, Varney could not resist putting a hand out to stop a pass reaching Joe Cokanasiga and a try in the corner.The penalty try was awarded and the Italy number nine sin-binned and with a man extra, replacement flanker Hill bulldozed his way to the line and with Russell adding the extras, they had more than a one-score cushion.Henry Slade missed one penalty to reduce the gap to six points, but Skinner stepped up in the 79th minute from the 40-metre line as Exeter pragmatically made sure they collected a losing bonus point to go with one for scoring four tries, while Bath have a maximum 10 from their two opening wins.Bath director of rugby Johann van Graan told BBC Radio Somerset:"It was a crazy game of rugby once again, Bath versus Exeter. We started the game really well but then they came out punching after half-time and scored three unanswered tries."But then that's why this game is a 23-man effort as we then came back with the impact of our eight (subs) who made a really good difference, so I'm really happy with the five points."We're very proud of our bench and numbers 16 to 23 at this club are just as important as numbers one to 15."   Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Radio Devon:"The important emotion is I'm walking away going 'we've got a team here and we've got something to work with'."Last week was such a patchy performance (losing 45-24 to Gloucester) but today we showed a lot of good qualities."The qualities of being in a fight to the death, that's what Exeter Chiefs are about. Do you want to be perfect or do you want to be in a fight every single week? Well we'll be in a fight every single week."I'm quite happy with that, that's what we're good at and I saw that today."Bath: Donoghue; Cokanasiga, Lawrence, Redpath, de Glanville; Russell, van der Linde; Obano, Dunn, Stuart, Roux, Ewels (capt), Richards, Pepper, du Preez.Replacements: Frost, Kirk, Griffin, Hill, Reid, Carr-Smith, Ojomoh, Coetzee.  Exeter: Woodburn; Feyi-Waboso, Slade, Butt, Wyatt; Skinner, Varney; Burger, Yeandle, Iosefa-Scott, Wilson, Jenkins (capt), E Roots, James, Fisilau. Replacements: Gulley, Goodrick-Clarke, Tchumbadze, Beckerleg, Worley Brady, Wolstenholme, Haydon-Wood, Wimbush.Sin-bin: Varney (61)Referee: Luke Pearce

title: Man City guilty charges: Which clubs did 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?
description: Manchester City's spending power unquestionably changed the world football transfer market - their willingness to pay higher fees and wages meant pric
body: Manchester City's spending power unquestionably changed the world football transfer market - their willingness to pay higher fees and wages meant prices rose for everybody else too.And once the world knows that a club has a wedge of cash burning a hole in its pocket courtesy of City, it can be difficult to spend it.Asking prices may rise, and having an influx of money is no guarantee of it being well spent.For many of the teams to whom City paid the most during this time, the money did not work out particularly beneficially.Let's take a look at some of the more interesting cases.First up, Wolfsburg. They immediately signed winger Julian Draxler for about half the fee received for Kevin de Bruyne in 2016, as well as others including veteran defender Dante.Having lost De Bruyne, they dropped from second to eighth in the Bundesliga before narrowly avoiding relegation in the subsequent two seasons.And things did not go particularly well for second highest-ranked club Monaco either. The most direct replacements they signed following the sales of Benjamin Mendy and Bernardo Silva in the same summer to Manchester City - Terence Kongolo and Keita Balde - did not work out in the long run, and the team went from winning Ligue 1 and reaching the Champions League semi-finals to almost being relegated within two years.The club City purchased most players from in the 2009-18 period - Arsenal (four) - did not mount a serious Premier League title challenge during that time.Some clubs who did not receive payments from City could also argue that the spending of money from their "inflated" accounts compromised their chances.For example, Manchester City paid very similar totals to Benfica and Porto during the era, but nothing to Sporting, the club which makes up the big three in Portugal.Sporting did not win a title between 2009 and 2018. There are many reasons for that, but could one of them be the fact that their direct rivals received money from City that would perhaps not have been on offer had they followed football's financial rules?There are also some ancillary fees which reached clubs whom Manchester City did not deal with directly.Some players were subject to sell-on clauses, where the club City where buying the player from owed money to the previous team who owned the player.For example, Queens Park Rangers earned roughly £9m from Raheem Sterling's move to City from Liverpool in 2015.Barnsley took about £7m of the transfer fee paid to Everton for John Stones in 2016, and the Toffees also had to pass on about £2.5m to Wolves when Joleon Lescott moved to Manchester in 2009.The Sterling and Stones clauses were worth more than most players operating in the English Football League at that time, significantly strengthening the financial positions of QPR and Barnsley.To this day Barnsley have not sold a player for a higher amount than the fee they are believed to have received for Stones.But QPR have not returned to the Premier League and Barnsley dropped down to League One from the Championship after two seasons.Manchester City's spending during the time in which they were breaking the rules certainly had an enormous impact, on their own upward trajectory, the futures of other clubs around the world and the wider football economy.But the reality is that it is impossible to unweave the tapestry of football history during that time and since - too much has happened and there are too many indirect consequences.The effects of that spending will reverberate for years to come.

schema.headline: Man City guilty charges: Which clubs did 'inflated' money flow to in transfer market?

title: Super League Grand Final: Warrington and Wakefield battle to be winner number six
description: While this is Wakefield's first final and the same for many of their players, like coach Powell a select few have sampled the unique atmosphere of Old
body: While this is Wakefield's first final and the same for many of their players, like coach Powell a select few have sampled the unique atmosphere of Old Trafford for Super League's showpiece event.Tom Johnstone begrudgingly left Wakefield for Catalans in 2023 and reached the Grand Final in his first season, before rejoining Trinity in 2025.That night ended in disappointment with defeat by Wigan, so the 2026 final represents a second chance for the England winger to pick up the ring he so covets - although it will not be the most important ring in his life as he admits."It's going to be different in so many ways for me because as much as I loved Catalans, this is my team," Johnstone told BBC Radio 5 live."This has been my team for almost all of my career, and the team that gave me an opportunity 15 years ago as a youngster."So, this is special, this is the big one and it's probably going to be, if we get it done, the best night of my life. Sorry, after my wedding, my wife said. She said it has to be second to my wedding."Like Warrington, Wakefield have waited a long time to return to league glory, with a 58-year gap since their last title.That narrative is one of many utilised by both clubs as inspiration for this Grand Final encounter, with several on both sides.One story for Wakefield to thrive upon is the impending retirement of stalwart back-rower Jay Pitts.Born in Ossett and a graduate of the youth set-up at Wakefield, the 36-year-old has amassed just short of 200 appearances for Trinity across two spells bookending his career which will end once Saturday's final is done.Pitts has battled through this crucial period following a bicep injury, and his determination and leadership are integral to the spirit within the dressing room."After the Wigan game I just went into the changing rooms and said to him 'you know you get to play your final game at Old Trafford'. It's what dreams are made of," Powell added."While there's a few players leaving us for different reasons, for Pittsy retiring after his final game in rugby league - what better way for us all to do something special for him as a person?"He's been a phenomenal player, a warrior, and I know all the boys love him. He gets a fair bit of stick for how old he is but that comes to us all so I won't worry about that too much."It has been 71 years since Warrington last won a league title and it is their first trip to Old Trafford for eight years.In the Super League era, the Wire have now reached five Grand Finals, but are yet to cross the line and write their name on the trophy.For Ben Currie, he is acutely aware of the gap between trophies, having been with the club during their four other visits - albeit he is yet to actually a appear in a Grand Final."It's hard not to know about it when you've got the opposite fans singing about it every week," he told BBC Radio Merseyside."Obviously it's tongue in cheek and it's fun for the fans to do that."We'd love to give our fans the opportunity to sing back to them but there's no added pressure from anyone from above in the club, from the coaching staff or from the senior players."Everyone wants it just the same as everyone does at Wakefield."One member of the Warrington team who could make an impact is 18-year-old Ewan Irwin.Since making his debut in 2025, Irwin has gone on to make 21 appearances this season, scoring six tries and kicking 82 goals.Matty Ashton, who himself was a bright young prospect for the Wire not so long ago, spoke highly of his team-mate, who has the chance to become the youngest player to ever score in a Grand Final."You see him day in and day out, his work ethic, he's probably the best I've seen in a young lad [and] obviously I've been at the club for seven years," Ashton said of Irwin to BBC Radio Merseyside."The way he's willing to learn when he speaks to leaders like George [Williams], it's just great to see."He's just got that something, you can see it. Obviously I don't want to put too much pressure as he's my team-mate, but he'll go all the way and he's got a big chance to do something like that."Warrington name a squad with just one change in their line-up.Jordy Crowther comes into the squad, with Max Wood dropping out.Wakefield, meanwhile, are unchanged following their dramatic semi-final win against Wigan Warriors.Josh Rourke is once again named in their provisional squad as he continues his return from a knee injury sustained in August.Warrington (from): Taylor-Wray, Thewlis, King, Hopoate, Ashton, Williams, Yates, Walker, Harrison, Stone, Currie, Powell, Byrne, Crowther, Irwin, Hayes, Bentley, Philbin, Lindop, Smith, Tanginoa.Wakefield (from): Jowitt, Scott, Hall, Johnstone, Trueman, Lino, McMeeken, Smoothy, Rodwell, Tevaga, Pitts, Hamlin-Uele, Faatili, Smith, Vagana, Walmsley, Sinfield, Myers, Rourke, Lolesio, Lipowicz.

title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
description: The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to gover
body: The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.The party said it would cost £2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early, under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: "A violent criminal doesn't become less dangerous just because the government has run out of prison cells."She added: "[Labour's] answer is to let dangerous offenders out even earlier instead of building the prison spaces we need."Labour Party chairwoman Bridget Phillipson said: "The Tories are taking the public for fools. Across 14 years in government, they added just 500 prison places and closed 23 prisons. "Now Kemi Badenoch expects the British people to believe they'll build 50,000."Meanwhile, the Prison Governors' Association said "long-term investment" was needed and warned a "staffing crisis" would pose challenges to delivering new prisons.If the party wins power, the Tories said they would introduce legislation early in the new Parliament to override planning and procurement barriers, allowing the process to be "fast-tracked".It said the use of private finance would help speed up delivery and control costs.There are currently around 89,000 useable prison places in England and Wales, according to the latest government figures.The Tories said their proposals would increase this figure by more than 50%, with the vast majority of new places expected within the party's first Parliament in government - up to five years - and the full increase delivered within seven years.The £2bn a year cost would be funded through savings in other areas, including cutting the aid budget by £1bn and reducing the budget of the Department for Culture Media and Sport by £1bn.The Labour government has promised to add 14,000 extra prison space by 2031.The Tories argued increasing prison places would cut crime and prevent reoffending by keeping serious criminals off the streets.Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said: "Prison works. It works by punishing and deterring, but most importantly by incapacitating. "Prison should keep violent and repeat offenders away from the law-abiding public."

schema.headline: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
